title: PHOENIX - ECP: Extracorporeal PHotopheresis for immune-related cOlitis and/or hEpatitis in advanced melaNoma with inadequate response to steroId eXposure
official: PHOENIX - ECP: A Phase 2, Randomized, Controlled, Open-label, Multicenter Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety/Tolerability of Extracorporeal Photopheresis (ECP) Versus Best Available Therapy (BAT) for the Treatment of Immune-related Colitis and/or Hepatitis with Inadequate Response to Corticosteroids in Participants with Unresectable or Metastatic Melanoma Treated with Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors (ICI)
summary: Main objective: To evaluate the efficacy of ECP in the treatment of ir-colitis and ir-hepatitis by assessing corticosteroid-free response.
conditions:
Immune-related Colitis or Hepatitis with Inadequate Response to Corticosteroids in
Participants with Unresectable or Metastatic Melanoma Treated with Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors (ICI)

interventions.name: UVADEX 20 micrograms/ml solution for blood fraction modification

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Be adequately informed and understand the nature and risks of the study and must be able to provide a signature and date on the informed consent form (ICF).
2. Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status 0, 1 or 2.
3. Life expectancy > 4 months.
4. Has adequate peripheral or central venous access to undergo ECP treatment.
5. Participants of non-childbearing potential OR participants using highly effective methods of contraception (see Appendix 4).
6. Participants whose sexual partner may become pregnant must use condoms or other methods to ensure effective contraception with partner, and abstain from donating blood, semen, or sperm during the study and for 90 days after the last study treatment (ECP or BAT; see Appendix 4).
7. State willingness to comply with all study procedures and availability for the duration of the study.
8. Adult (age ≥ 18 years) persons of any sex and gender.
9. Diagnosed with unresectable or metastatic melanoma (eg, Stage III and Stage IV).
10. Received ICI treatment (eg, anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, anti-LAG-3, anti-CTLA-4 antibody, as ICI monotherapy or ICI combination therapy).
11. ICI paused or discontinued because of the development of ir-colitis or ir-hepatitis.
12. Diagnosed with ir-colitis or ir-hepatitis with a severity of Grade 2 or higher, based on ASCO Guidelines (ir-colitis: diarrhea with an increase of ≥ 4 stools more than at baseline with other potential causes of diarrhea and colitis ruled out by the appropriate evaluations; ir-hepatitis: increase in AST or ALT > 3 × upper limit of normal, total bilirubin > 1.5 × ULN, or alkaline phosphatase > 2.5 × ULN, after exclusion of other potential causes of hepatotoxicity and ruling out the increase is due to development or progression of liver metastases; pre-existing liver metastases are not exclusionary).
13. For participant with ir-colitis: Endoscopic evidence of ir-colitis based on colonoscopy, as performed within 10 days prior to randomization.
14. Has inadequate response to corticosteroids, defined as: a. No improvement in ir-colitis or ir-hepatitis after at least 72 hours of treatment with systemic corticosteroids (corticosteroid-refractory), OR b. Relapse of ir-colitis or ir-hepatitis (back to Grade 2 or higher) during or after corticosteroid tapering (corticosteroid-dependent).
Exclusion criteria:
1. irAEs in addition to and other than ir-colitis or ir-hepatitis, with a higher severity grade than the irAE for inclusion (ir-colitis/ir-hepatitis) based on ASCO guidelines (see Appendix 1 and Appendix 2).
2. Known allergic reaction to any component of 8-methoxsalen, infliximab, vedolizumab, MMF or azathioprine.
3. Has aphakia or a history of light sensitive diseases such as lupus erythematosus, porphyria cutanea tarda, erythropoietic protoporphyria, variegate porphyria, xeroderma pigmentosum, and albinism.
4. Hemodynamically unstable, requires vasopressors, and/or has New York Heart Association class III or IV heart failure, uncontrolled hypertension, or ventricular arrhythmias.
5. Unable to tolerate the fluid shift associated with the ECP procedure.
6. Participants with a history of human immunodeficiency virus or a positive result on human immunodeficiency virus
7. Positive result for tuberculosis testing (blood testing).
8. Positive result for active or previous viral hepatitis B, or active hepatitis C testing at screening.
9. Positive screening test for Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), cytomegalovirus (CMV), or adenovirus.
10. Active coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) infection.
11. Prior allogeneic bone marrow transplantation or prior solid organ transplantation.
12. Has a diagnosis of uveal melanoma as the sole melanoma subtype (ie, without a diagnosis of cutaneous, acral or mucosal melanoma).
13. Any active malignancies, other than unresectable or metastatic melanoma.
14. Previous splenectomy.
15. Concurrent treatment with another investigational drug, device, or other investigational intervention.
16. Any condition that would, in the investigator's judgment, interfere with full participation in the study, including administration of study treatment and attending required study visits poses a significant risk to the participant; or interfere with interpretation of study data.
17. Inability to operate electronic devices such as a smart phone  to complete patient diaries and questionnaires.
18. Treatment of ir-colitis or ir-hepatitis with any systemic therapy other than corticosteroids.
19. Concurrent conditions which may require treatment with high dose corticosteroid (> 1 mg/kg/day) and interfere with the corticosteroid tapering schedule recommended by the protocol.
20. Pre-existing liver disease (eg, primary autoimmune hepatitis, primary sclerosing cholangitis, primary biliary cholangitis). Isolated low titer autoantibody positivity or mild immunoglobulin G elevation in the setting of hepatic metastases or malignancy-related inflammation, without other evidence of autoimmune hepatitis, will not be considered exclusionary.
21. Active alcohol use disorder (per investigator assessment and/or Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, 5th Edition criteria).
22. Concomitant treatment with any chemotherapy or targeted therapy for the treatment of unresectable or metastatic melanoma.
23. Use of any investigational agent within 5 half-lives of the investigational agent prior to randomization.
24. Any known contraindications to study intervention and/or procedures (methoxalen, the ECP procedure, infliximab or vedolizumab, MMF or azathioprine).
